genesis.43.p1.b1.text: Go back and buy us a little more food.

genesis.43.p1.b2.text: The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’

genesis.43.p1.b3.text: Why did you bring this trouble upon me? … Why did you tell the man you had another brother?

genesis.43.p1.b4.text: The man questioned us in detail about ourselves and our family … How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother here’?

genesis.43.p2.b1.text: I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.

genesis.43.p2.b2.text: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man—a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.

genesis.43.p2.b3.text: Take double the silver with you … Perhaps it was a mistake.

genesis.43.p2.b4.text: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man … As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.

genesis.43.p3.b1.text: So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

genesis.43.p3.b2.text: Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.

genesis.43.p3.b3.text: The man did as Joseph had commanded and took the brothers to Joseph’s house.

genesis.43.p4.b1.text: We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time … They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves

genesis.43.p4.b2.text: Please, sir … each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.

genesis.43.p4.b3.text: It is fine … Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks.

genesis.43.p4.b4.text: Then he brought Simeon out to them.

genesis.43.p5.b1.text: And the steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their donkeys.

genesis.43.p5.b2.text: they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon.

genesis.43.p5.b3.text: How is your elderly father you told me about? Is he still alive?

genesis.43.p5.b4.text: Your servant our father is well … He is still alive.

genesis.43.p6.b1.text: Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?

genesis.43.p6.b2.text: May God be gracious to you, my son.

genesis.43.p7.b1.text: Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother,

genesis.43.p7.b2.text: and he went to a private room to weep.

genesis.43.p7.b3.text: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”

genesis.43.p8.b1.text: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians.

genesis.43.p8.b2.text: the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.

genesis.43.p8.b3.text: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest,

genesis.43.p8.b4.text: and the men looked at one another in astonishment.

genesis.43.p9.b1.text: When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table,

genesis.43.p9.b2.text: Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others.

genesis.43.p9.b3.text: So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.
